newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rates jump, traders surprised.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rates jump, traders surprised.

text.p: * Turnover higher at 23.254 bln pesos from 20.580 bln
Philippine interbank call loan rates jumped to an average of 12.5625 percent on Tuesday from 11.46875, surprising many traders.

They said banks were anticipating to be short of only one billion pesos this week. Outflows from the system have been estimated at 5.5 billion pesos from investment in T-bills and notes, while inflows in the amount of 4.6 billion pesos are expected from maturing T-bills.

Though banks were expected to remain open, they were also beefing up liquidity positions to prepare for the higher spending during the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) holidays from November 22 to 26, other traders said.
"We're still trying to find out why (rates went up). There may have an overinvestment in reverse repos after money market rates stabilised last week," a big bank trader said.
Rates shot to a high of 15 percent, with the low at 11.0625. Out of the 58 participating financial insitutions, 27 were lenders.
In the secondary market for T-bills, there was not much appetite to buy T-bills after rates fell in the primary auction on Monday, traders said.
Trading was focused on the long-term T-notes where rates were more attractive, traders said.
Dealers said the three-month bill was being quoted an offer rate of 11.625 to 11.75, the six months at 12.20 to 12.275; and the one year at 12.60 to 12.725.
